predecessors.name: Jin dynasty (Western and Eastern Jin)
predecessors.text: the Jin realm of 417-425 without the land Xia held from 418: Guanzhong, Anding, and the Weibei-Longdong land that the Cliopatria Xia 426 shape draws north of the Qinling ('the Chang'an region became…

successors.name: Southern Qi
successors.text: the whole Liu Song realm, taken by Xiao Daocheng, who 'took the throne himself and declared himself Emperor of Qi' in 479

ledger.x: 420: Liu Yu takes the Jin throne at Jiankang and founds the Liu Song.
422: the Wei invade the Song lands south of the Yellow River.
423: Luoyang and the lands south of the Yellow River pass to the Wei.
430: Dao Yanzhi's army recovers Luoyang, Hulao, Huatai and Qiao'ao.
431: the Wei retake the four cities.
431: the Wei hold again the lands south of the Yellow River that they took in 422-423; the next fighting is the Song invasion of late 450.
435: Feng Hong of the Northern Yan becomes a Song vassal.
436: the vassalage ends with the Northern Yan.
446: Tan Hezhi's Liu Song army takes and plunders the Lâm Ấp capital.
446: the Song army withdraws with its plunder.
450: Emperor Wen invades the Wei lands.
451: the Wei withdraw from the Yangtze.
466: Liu Song's northern governors defect to the Wei after Liu Zixun's rising.
466: Xu and Yan Provinces go to the Wei.
468: Murong Baiyao takes Qing and Ji Provinces.
468: the recovery attempts end; the Song north-east is Wei land.
479: Xiao Daocheng ends the Liu Song and founds the Qi.

wars.name: Northern Wei invasion of Liu Song, 422-423
wars.outcome: The Wei take the provinces south of the Yellow River (Luoyang, Hulao, Xuchang, Sizhou, Yanzhou in the northern-wei dossier).

wars.name: Dao Yanzhi's expedition and the Wei counter-attack, 430-431
wars.outcome: The Song recover Luoyang, Hulao, Huatai and Qiao'ao in 430 and lose them again by spring 431.

wars.name: Liu Song invasion of Lâm Ấp
wars.outcome: Tan Hezhi captures and plunders the capital of Lâm Ấp in February 446; no annexation is recorded.

wars.name: Liu Song-Northern Wei war of 450-451
wars.outcome: The Song invasion of late 450 fails; the Wei reach Guabu on the Yangtze around the new year 451 and withdraw in spring 451.

wars.name: Liu Song campaign of 452
wars.outcome: 'Emperor Wen made another attempt to destroy Northern Wei in 452, but failed again'; Zhang Yong was defeated at Qiao'ao and the campaign abandoned.

wars.name: Loss of the north-east: Liu Zixun's rising and the defection of Xu, Yan, Qing and Ji, 466-468
wars.outcome: Xu and Yan Provinces defect in 466 and are lost for good in autumn 467; Qing and Ji fall to Murong Baiyao in spring 468.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line appears on any page opened: the Yellow River and Huai fronts are approximate, and the provinces of the far south (Lingnan, Jiaozhou) are drawn as Cliopatria has them.
